title: Growing Ziebert-Aranson crawlers divide when a weak finite-range (Ohta-Kawasaki) area penalty is added: founder to gen 4 with 0 merges, but the population jams into a static crystal
summary: Same world as the positive control, run with WORLD_P from params.json: each body's target area V grows by uptake of a consumed, regrowing nutrient (V carried between steps by u-weighted overlap, shared by area at a split), and delta gets an extra term lamOK*(G_ell*u - Mref) applied only inside bodies (Gaussian kernel ell=10, about the cell radius). A single crawling founder grows into a crescent that tears into several crawling daughters (t=25-80), which spread as a ring wave and keep dividing: max generation 4, 10 persistent splits, 0 merges on both seeds 0 and 1 (pack/). Without the finite-range term the same growth gives one ever-larger crawler and no division (parent sighting); with the finite-range term as the only constraint the cell expands radially, breaks up and freezes into a hexagonal tiling with no crawling (neg_local_only/). Limits: after t~300 the population fills the domain and becomes a jammed, nearly static packing; lowering nutrient regrowth (rn 0.003, neg_lowfeed/) just gives a smaller static crystal, cells stop crawling once round and starved and do not die; labkit reports 19 'nucleations' per seed that I have not yet traced (likely dim fragments crossing threshold).
